prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Adverse Weather Mode (Duty Manager may reduce remote stand use), Recovery Phase (remote stands absorb late arrivals, contact gates kept for tight turnarounds), Capacity Reduction State (Business Rules Registry may tighten escalation thresholds, suppress low-impact issues), Contingency Fallback State (exception summaries via Contingency Operations Console). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; persistent remote stand limits = reduced gate throughput); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; exceptions after Registry materiality; remote stand constraints); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display shows remote stand status in time order; Collaborative Decision Log; records remote stand reason, flights, transfer duration, control position); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft unless remote stand release supports taxi plan); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo; contact gate vs remote stand delay); Airline Interface Adapter (Late Baggage Tag List to Ground Handling Dispatcher); Handling Resource Planner (Remote Stand Shuttle Count); Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet surface advisory latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s); Audit Event Ledger (MUST record adjustments, actors, overrides, exceptions; Identity Access Service); Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet); Performance Analytics Warehouse (thresholds; remote stand timing); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Digital Briefing Room. Remote stand departure ready only when passengers, bags, crew, services aligned. Flight record has border release readiness attribute; customs hold blocks stand release/readiness. Actors: Airport Duty Manager (Medical Diversion Notice; Customs Hold Release Note; remote stand posture), Regional

New part:
S570: A flight under a customs hold may remain physically parked and technically serviceable while still being unavailable for normal passenger, baggage, or crew movement decisions.
S571: When border release status is unknown, the Demand Prediction Service treats the turnaround milestone as uncertain rather than assuming that the planned connection interval is valid.
S572: The Airport CDM Portal displays border and customs status in a controlled view so that only authorized operational users see the clearance condition needed for coordination.
S573: The Regional Flow Manager uses aggregated border delay exposure to decide whether an arrival regulation should be adjusted or whether delay absorption should remain local to the airport.
S574: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses customs hold visibility to adjust connection protection, passenger messaging assumptions, and expected aircraft turnaround timing.
S575: The Slot Allocation Engine treats an unresolved customs hold as a reason to avoid assigning an aggressive departure sequence position to the affected flight.
S576: The Arrival Regulation Console uses the Medical Diversion Notice to protect arrival priority, stand assignment timing, and downstream border coordination in the active arrival plan.
S577: Customs status changes are time stamped before they are used in sequencing so that operational decisions are based on the latest authoritative clearance state.
S578: The East Apron Sensor reports stand occupancy transitions, pushback lane blockage durations, and sensor confidence values at a synchronized event time.
S579: West Apron Sensor observations are used to verify whether remote stand areas and service roads are actually available for the traffic pattern shown in the plan.
S580: The Surface Surveillance Adapter normalizes apron sensing data into movement, occupancy, and blockage events that can be correlated with flight milestones.
S581: The Ramp Movement Board presents apron sensor events as operational evidence for stand release, taxi lane availability, and vehicle conflict assessment.
S582: The Gate Conflict Detector uses border status and apron occupancy evidence to distinguish a true gate conflict from a temporary clearance delay.
S583: The Tower Sequence Manager considers confirmed apron blockage when determining whether a departure can be included in the next practical movement sequence.
S584: The Capacity Assessment Module applies persistent apron congestion as a local capacity factor when estimating achievable departure throughput during Normal Operations and Adverse Weather Mode.
S585: The Time Synchronization Service is required because customs status events and apron sensor events must align with Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time decisions.
S586: The Business Rules Registry defines which border and customs states block sequencing, which states require human confirmation, and which states are informational only.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
